overall._posture: Synthesized coverage from 2023 b10 schema, data dictionary, sample JSON, and workflow description. Rejected `insufficiently_documented` because artifact depth is high and rejected `projection_limited` because native multi-domain evidence is broader than a pure USCDI slice. Certainty high.
overall._completenessScore: Set to 4 because major clinical and financial domains are represented directly, while low-confidence modules (telehealth/intake/audit) are not clearly represented. Certainty high.
overall._technicalUsabilityScore: Set to 4 because schema + sample + readable instructions materially reduce implementation burden; missing enums and relationship semantics reduce but do not block ingestion. Certainty high.

overall._strongestSignal: Used three artifact types together: machine-readable schema, field-description XLSX, and complete single-patient sample JSON ZIP, all aligned on the same native JSON model. Certainty high.
overall.strongestSignal: Schema + dictionary + sample are coherent and cover both clinical and practice management entities.
overall._biggestRisk: Missing value semantics and limited visibility into custom modules/telehealth/intake attachments create the highest migration risk, not the absence of core schemas. Certainty high.
overall.biggestRisk: Weak value constraints and potentially unmodeled specialty/custom artifacts could cause silent semantic drift in downstream mapping.
overall._summary: OfficeEMR provides a broad native export surface with practical self-service for single-patient use and assisted bulk migration support. The export is usable, but conservatively treated as partial because some workflows are only indirectly represented and full coding semantics are under-documented.
overall.summary: Practical for migration projects with strong implementation effort but needs a supplemental validation run for specialty, portal, and telehealth edge data.

notableFacts: Collected artifacts are explicitly for OfficeEMR (`officeemr.knowledgeowl.com/help/ehi-export`) and include native JSON schema, field dictionary, and sample output.
Single-patient export is UI-triggered and role-gated, with direct ZIP download when completed.
Practice export is role-restricted and documented as a backlog process involving the vendor data export team (about 15 days).
Schema files are machine-readable but `description` fields in JSON Schema are largely empty; the XLSX dictionary carries semantic descriptions.
No explicit value-set or enum definitions were found in collected evidence.
No export entities for audit/access logs were found in the EHI schema/sample set.
